column3: The library every program sees without importing it: numbers, arrays, sorting, heaps, strings, parsing, printing and random numbers.
Rounding, roots, trigonometry, exponentials and logarithms for `real` and `f32` values, plus `PI` and `TAU`.
Small fixed vectors such as `float3` with dot and cross products, lengths, normalizing and blending.
A hash map from any key type to any value type, with insert, lookup, update, remove and iteration.
Try a block of code and throw a value out of any depth beneath it.
Write JSON text, read it piece by piece with a pull reader, or parse it into a small document tree.
Regular expressions over bytes. Matching time grows linearly with the text, so a bad pattern cannot hang a program.
Encode and decode Base64 text.
Float bit patterns, bounds-checked little-endian reads, a read cursor and little-endian writes.
Decompress DEFLATE and zlib streams, the compression used inside PNG files.
Files, folders, standard streams, command-line arguments, environment variables, clocks and child processes.
Read raw memory at addresses handed over by foreign code such as C libraries.
The GPU layer: windows, input events, buffers, textures, samplers, render passes, pipelines and compute.
A 3D renderer for glTF assets with sun shadows, ambient occlusion, temporal upscaling, bloom and color grading.
Load glTF 2.0 models (`.glb` and `.gltf`) into memory pools the renderer uploads in one go.
Build spheres, planes and boxes in code. They render through `gfx.scene3d` exactly like loaded models.
Pose glTF scenes: sample animation channels, walk the node tree, and build joint matrices and morph weights.
Quaternions, rigid transforms and 4x4 matrix helpers for the 3D renderer.
GPU particle emitters that spawn, simulate, sort and draw.
Fast GPU particles drawn as glowing camera-facing discs in the `gfx.scene3d` color pass.
Build a bounding volume tree of triangles for ray tracing, upload it to the GPU, and test rays against it.
Pick and apply graphics quality settings for the device.
Decode PNG files to RGBA pixels and write 8-bit PNG files.
Decode baseline JPEG files to RGBA pixels.
The classic Cornell box test scene as plain triangle data.
A full interface toolkit: windows, layouts, buttons, sliders, text editing, charts, trees, fonts and styling.
An in-game HUD: a tree of nodes with layout, animated tweens, rich text and localized strings.
A built-in font drawn from vector strokes, so text stays sharp at any size with no font files.
Turn raw touch input into gestures.
Read TrueType fonts: metrics, glyph shapes, glyph bitmaps and packing glyphs into atlases.
Load and play sounds with voices, 3D positioning, mix buses, reverb and offline rendering.
The clip bank: keyframes at a uniform rate, sampled by time or phase, with additive clips and root motion.
Skeletons, local poses, forward kinematics, blending, additive layers and per-bone masks.
1D and 2D blend spaces that turn values such as speed into weights over sample clips.
The animation state machine: states, conditional transitions, crossfades, phase sync and interruption.
Two-bone and FABRIK chain inverse kinematics, plus a foot-planting helper.
Skinning palettes and linear-blend skinning of glTF mesh data on the CPU.
Linear-blend skinning on the GPU through a self-contained Vulkan compute backend.
Read skinned characters from `.glb` files: skeletons, inverse bind matrices and animation samplers.
Quaternions and rigid transforms for the animation runtime.
A ready-made walking and running character: speed blending, action states, an upper-body layer, root motion and foot planting.
A 3D rigid-body physics engine: worlds, bodies, shapes, joints, contacts, queries and recordings.
Build a navigation mesh of walkable cells and find paths across it.
Stream a large world: load and unload grid cells in background threads as the player moves.
The core of a scene editor: entities, undo and redo, parenting, save and load, picking and drag handles.
Connect an edited scene to the 3D renderer so it draws in the viewport.
TCP and UDP sockets with addresses, polling, length-prefixed frames and readable error names.
Minimal IPv4 UDP sockets.
Non-blocking TCP client connections with host name lookup.
An HTTP client with chunked replies and JSON helpers.
A TLS client with certificate checking and pinning.
A WebSocket client.
A Socket.IO client over WebSocket, with a fallback to long polling.
Reliable and unreliable game messages over UDP, with acknowledgments and round-trip timing.
Compact game-state snapshots, interpolation and client-side prediction.
SHA-1 and SHA-2 hashes, HMAC, HKDF, PBKDF2 and constant-time comparison.
Authenticated encryption with ChaCha20-Poly1305 and AES-GCM.
X25519 key exchange and Ed25519 signatures.
Elliptic-curve keys, ECDH key exchange, and ECDSA signing and verification.
RSA PKCS#1 and PSS signature verification.
Parse X.509 certificates and verify certificate chains.
Big-number and Montgomery arithmetic the other security modules build on.
Secure random bytes from the operating system.
Fast GF(2^8) arithmetic over byte buffers and the AES S-box and MixColumns steps, using CPU vector instructions when present.
Talk to the browser from a Helium web build: page elements, events, timers, fetch, storage and other JavaScript libraries.
WebGL2 graphics on a canvas: shaders, buffers, textures and draw calls.
Assigns scene lights to a 3D grid of view-frustum cells so renderers can efficiently shade many lights per pixel.
Decodes Radiance HDR (RGBE) image files into floating-point pixel data, letting a program load high-dynamic-range images.
Encodes RGBA pixel images into JPEG-compressed byte data, with adjustable quality, so programs can save or send photos.
Lets a program load environment maps and prefilter them into GGX-blurred cubemaps for image-based lighting, including sun and haze effects.
Converts numbers to JavaScript-style strings, including formatting with fixed decimals and locale-aware digit grouping.
Lets a program convert text and JSON values into integers and floats using Python-style parsing rules, including whitespace and underscores.
Decodes BC1, BC3, BC4, BC5, and BC7 block-compressed texture data into raw RGBA pixels and computes compressed sizes.
Parses KTX2 texture files, validating headers and reading dimensions, color space, and mip levels for block-compressed or raw images.
Builds meshlets from triangle meshes by welding vertices and grouping triangles into clusters and hierarchy levels for efficient rendering.
Simulates cloth as a mesh of particles with gravity, drag, and collisions so fabric drapes and moves realistically.
